class: cross-file contract (git check-ignore semantics vs capture staging mode)
golden_cause: Checkpoint capture decides the workspace is ignored by running `git check-ignore --no-index` on `.` and treating an empty result as ignored; a blank CRLF or whitespace-only line in any ignore source matches `./`, so a normal workspace looks ignored, capture stages with `git add -u` instead of `-A`, untracked files are left out of the checkpoint, and a later restore deletes them.
other_side: apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:1038 (consumer `workspaceIgnored ? "-u" : "-A"`; probe helper filterIgnoredPaths at :700-712 runs `check-ignore --no-index`)
note: added apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:969: const workspaceIgnored = (yield* filterIgnoredPaths(input.cwd, ["."])).length === 0; and added :1038: workspaceIgnored ? "-u" : "-A", (the check-ignore helper itself at :708 is pre-existing; this PR adds the "." probe and its consumer). Candidate re-check: PASSES (4 files). Bots on intro: summary comments only.

class: cross-file contract (message origin vs startup recovery filter)
golden_cause: The usage-limit auto-resume command was switched from createdBy "user" to "agent", but startup recovery keeps only createdBy === "user" queued messages; if the server restarts after the resume is dispatched and before the provider starts it, recovery cancels the run and the worker rebuilds the same limit-resume command id (already receipted), so the auto-resume never comes back and nothing tells the user.
note: added UsageLimitRecoveryWorker.ts:76: createdBy: "agent", (changed from "user"). Fix PR #31292 body names this PR as the regression source. Bots on intro: summary/approval only.

golden_cause: settleAfterRun waits for the agent's run to end and then dispatches `thread.settle` exactly once; if a background notification or delegated completion starts another run first, the server refuses the settle (active or queued run) and the dispatch is dropped, so the thread the agent asked to settle stays active forever.

golden_cause: Each tool-output update event is charged to the live-stream byte budget when retained, before superseded updates for the same thread, run and tool are coalesced away at flush, so a burst of large updates for one tool raises LiveStreamBufferError and disconnects the slow client even though only the latest update would be sent.

class: cross-file contract (desktop main process vs renderer prompt lifetime)
golden_cause: The renderer now keeps SSH password prompts in a module-level queue for the life of the page, appended on each desktop prompt event and removed only by the user's submit or cancel; when the main process ends a prompt (timeout, cancel, window close) the renderer is never told, so the ended prompt stays on screen and later prompts stack behind it.
